merges.document:
REQ-1: Send a delay notification when the carrier's latest ETA is more than 2 hours after the promised delivery time. Exactly 2 hours late does not trigger.
REQ-2: Trust only the carrier's latest ETA, which arrives in UTC. Compare it with the promised time as absolute instants. Show all times to the customer in the delivery address's local time, with the date.
REQ-3: Send at most 2 notifications per shipment. The first is sent when REQ-1 is met. The second is sent only if a later ETA is at least 2 hours after the ETA shown in the first notification; that ETA is the baseline. Q3 says 'slips by a further 2 hours', so exactly 2 hours further triggers. This differs from the 'more than' rule in Q1 and needs confirmation.
REQ-4: Always evaluate the carrier's latest ETA only. After the second notification, send nothing more for that shipment.
AC-1: The address is at UTC+2 (illustrative) and the promised time is 14:00 local (12:00 UTC). A carrier ETA of 14:01 UTC is 2h01m late, so one notification is sent showing 16:01 local.
AC-2: Same shipment, but the carrier ETA is 14:00 UTC, exactly 2h00m late. No notification is sent.
AC-3: After AC-1's notification (baseline ETA 14:01 UTC, 16:01 local), a new ETA of 16:00 UTC (18:00 local) is 1h59m further, so nothing is sent. A new ETA of 16:01 UTC (18:01 local) is exactly 2h further and sends the second notification. Any later ETA sends nothing.
AC-4: The address is at UTC+2 and the promised time is 1 March 23:00 local (21:00 UTC). A carrier ETA of 2 March 00:30 UTC is 3h30m late. A notification is sent showing 2 March 02:30 local, not 00:30 or 1 March.

claude.reason: Both versions are correct and address both findings, but Version 1 is marginally better because AC-3 also checks that the second notification shows 18:01 local time, so the conversion rule is tested there too.

grok.reason: Both versions add a non-UTC date-rollover test and state the first-notice ETA as the slip baseline, and every figure and rule checks out.

draft.text:
REQ-1. Notify if carrier latest UTC ETA means delivery >2h after promised time in delivery address local time.
REQ-2. Send at most 2 notifications per shipment: initial delay then only if slips further 2h.
AC-1. Promised 2024-10-05 14:00 local; ETA 2024-10-05 17:30 UTC (local 16:30) sends 1st notice.
AC-2. Later ETA 2024-10-05 20:00 UTC (local 19:00) sends 2nd notice.

verdicts.reason: Both drafts are arithmetically correct. Draft 1 is preferred because it tests the exact 2-hour boundaries for both the first notice and the further slip and caps notices at two. Its weakness is that it uses a zero UTC offset, whereas Draft 2 actually exercises the UTC-to-local conversion but omits boundary and no-third-notice cases.

Draft 1 better matches the facts by stating every rule and correctly testing the strict more-than-2-hour threshold, an exact further 2-hour second notice, and the two-notice cap, while Draft 2 only uses over-threshold examples and is less complete.

review.text:
D-A1 · P0 · Wrong threshold in AC-1
  AC-1 states a 14:01 UTC ETA is 2h01m late from 12:00 UTC promised but this is actually a 2h01m delay; brief and Q1 require more than 2 hours after promised time to trigger, and exactly 2 hours must not trigger per REQ-1, but the example violates the 2-hour threshold rule.
D-A2 · P0 · Incorrect date handling in AC-4
  Promised 1 March 23:00 local (21:00 UTC), ETA 2 March 00:30 UTC is exactly 3.5 hours late but AC-4 claims 3h30m late which recomputes correctly only if dates align; notification must show 2 March 02:30 local per REQ-2 but example date math was not independently recomputed per rules.
D-A3 · P1 · Unconfirmed assumption on exactly 2h
  REQ-3 assumes 'more than' for the further 2-hour slip matching Q1 but explicitly notes this needs confirmation; draft must only use confirmed facts without flagging unconfirmed logic per rules to avoid stating uncertain rules.
Strengths: AC-2 correctly applies the more-than-2-hours rule by not notifying on an exact 2h00m delay.

verdicts.reason: Review 1 is more useful: the draft checks out (AC-1 12:00 to 14:01 UTC is 2h01m late, shown as 16:01 local; AC-2 is exactly 2h00m and correctly silent; AC-3 has 16:01 UTC exactly 2h further and silent, 16:02 UTC triggers, 18:01 and 18:02 local; AC-4 21:00 UTC 1 March to 00:30 UTC 2 March is 3h30m, shown as 02:30 local 2 March), while all three Review 2 findings are wrong: D-A1 contradicts itself, D-A2 confirms the math it calls incorrect, and D-A3 faults a properly flagged open question.
Review 1 correctly finds no defects, while all three Review 2 findings invent problems in examples and an assumption note that match the stated rules.
